name: R Draconis
what_it_is: a Mira variable: a cool giant star that pulsates, growing brighter and fainter with a regular period

notes: Saturated in 2471 of 2471 images (OVERFLOW flag or empty core): too bright for SPHEREx, so no spectrum of the star itself is shown.

light_curve.what_is_plotted: a relative brightness index from the outer glow of the star image (not a magnitude), because the star is too bright for the detectors' cores
notes: Period search (100–1000 d) on the index: best period 246 d (W1) and 247 d (W2), matching the known Mira period of 245.6 d (GCVS).
WISE visits this star only about every 6 months, so an alias period near 713 d fits almost as well; the data are consistent with the known period but could not single it out without it.
Folded on 245.6 d, one sine wave explains 75 % of the W1 index variation (semi-amplitude 0.31 mag in the index).
NEOWISE profile-fit magnitudes of R Dra scatter by up to ~2 mag within single visits (beyond the saturation-correction range) and are not used.
SPHEREx points (synthesized at 3.4/4.6 µm from per-epoch spectra) are not possible: the star is saturated in SPHEREx.

what_to_look_for_in_the_movie: the star stays in place but its glow swells and shrinks as it pulsates
